relevance_note: Single-patient case report: 'Whole exome sequencing identified a heterozygous de novo pathogenic variant of the TNFAIP3 gene (c. 1777 C>T in exon 7, p.Q593X)'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; no tables. JSON assembled with a short script from hand-written values. In scope: the patient and her two parents (tested by WES, neither carries the variant; sex not stated individually, so labelled 'parent of patient' / 'parent of patient 2'; both get consanguinity 'yes' from 'Parental consanguinity was noted'). Grandmothers (sisters) are not tested or affected, so not in scope. Patients from reviews (Yu et al., Aeschlimann et al., Zhou et al.) appear only as counts: no rows. Somatic p.Q593X in MALT lymphoma/basal cell carcinoma (refs 14, 15) not recorded. Onset taken as 2.5 years (presentation with cervical lymphadenopathy, which the Discussion names among 'The initial features of HA20'); atopic dermatitis and infections in the first year of life precede it. Age at diagnosis not stated (referred to genetic counselor at age 14; age at WES result not given); provisional SLE diagnosis was made after flares at ages 8-11. Vital status not stated explicitly. Temporal contrasts, not treated as contradictions: complement C3/C4 normal at 7.5 years, suppressed during flares at 8-11, normal or elevated at 12-14; immunoglobulins normal-to-elevated at 7.5 years, low at 14. Both complement rows emitted. Oral and genital ulcers marked excluded from 'mucosal ulcers have not been a feature ... at any point in her life'; GI ulcers or inflammation left not reported. CSF pleocytosis during a hospitalization 'for concern of meningitis' recorded as a feature, but the checklist CNS item left not reported because the paper does not state CNS involvement. Cytopenia (autoimmune) marked observed from pancytopenia/thrombocytopenia with positive anti-platelet antibodies; the paper does not call the cytopenia autoimmune, and the neutropenia at 11 resolved after stopping MMF. Bronchiectasis is not ILD. Ferritin is not CRP/ESR, so inflammatory markers left not reported. Variant type 'nonsense' from the paper's 'premature stop codon'. Authors call the diagnosis presumptive (no functional assays).
